_about: The budgets are the definition of done (docs/decisions/004-budgets.md). The device lane is the oldest phone Stub supports, judged against Apple's guidance; the simulator lane is regression guards measured on the Stub Perf SE2 simulator on Bruno's Mac (Xcode 27.0, iOS 27.0). A ceiling may be tightened in any commit. Raising one needs a decision in docs/decisions saying why: never quietly. scripts/budgets.py judges a run against this file.

lanes.device: iPhone SE (2nd generation) or iPhone 11, A13, iOS 26: the oldest phone Stub supports; the model path on iPhone 15 Pro, the oldest with Apple Intelligence
lanes.simulator: Stub Perf SE2 simulator, iOS 27.0, on an Apple silicon Mac: regression guards, not the phone's numbers
lanes.ci: GitHub Actions' xcode-27 image, an iOS 27 simulator: regression guards calibrated on that machine from its first runs (a ceiling here is not this Mac's)

budgets.name: Cold launch to first frame
budgets.why: WWDC19 'Optimizing App Launch': render the first frame within 400 ms, the length of the launch animation.

budgets.name: Cold launch to responsive
budgets.why: The first frame plus Apple's 100 ms for a discrete action ('Improving app responsiveness'): ready for a thumb the moment it can see the drawer.

budgets.name: Drawer fling, tickets: hitch time ratio
budgets.why: WWDC20 'Eliminate animation hitches with XCTest': under 5 ms/s is good. The stricter of Apple's two published scales (Organizer's current page calls 10 good).

budgets.name: Drawer fling, tickets: CPU time
budgets.why: The work done per fling: the simulator records no hitches, so CPU time is its guard on what each frame costs.

budgets.name: Drawer fling, editions: hitch time ratio
budgets.why: As tickets: the heavier face has the same budget.

budgets.name: Drawer fling, editions: CPU time
budgets.why: Regression guard; first measured with this file.

budgets.name: Reveal: hitch time ratio
budgets.why: WWDC20: an animation interval under 5 ms/s of hitches.

budgets.name: Capture, rules: shutter to keepable
budgets.why: Decision 001's ten seconds from pocket to kept, broken down: about 1.5 s to the viewfinder, 3 s to frame and shoot, at most 1.5 s to read, 3 s to look and keep, 1 s spare.

budgets.name: Capture, rules: reader's last word
budgets.why: With no model, the rules' answer is the last word: a breath after keepable.

budgets.name: Capture, rules: Keep to saved
budgets.why: Apple: 100 ms for a discrete action ('Improving app responsiveness').

budgets.name: Capture, rules: Keep to the press on screen
budgets.why: Apple: 100 ms for a discrete action. Was 0.31 s on the simulator until the Aztec code moved off the main thread (decision 004).

budgets.name: Capture, model: shutter to keepable
budgets.why: The model never stands between the person and Keep (decision 001): the same budget as the rules.

budgets.name: Capture, model: reader's last word
budgets.why: Keepable plus the reader's 8 s patience plus half a second: by construction (StubReader.patience).

budgets.name: Capture, model: Keep to saved
budgets.why: Apple: 100 ms for a discrete action.

budgets.name: Keep to the printed card, by the clock
budgets.why: The press prints the edition pass by pass, about 1.2 s by design (ADR-015); the rest is the response.

budgets.name: Tilt-light: hitch time ratio
budgets.why: WWDC20: under 5 ms/s while the light moves.

budgets.name: Tilt-light: peak memory
budgets.why: Apple publishes no number. 200 MB is under a seventh of what a 3 GB phone allows one app, so Stub is not the app iOS ends first when it is in the background (WWDC18 'iOS Memory Deep Dive').

budgets.name: Tilt-light: CPU time over a 4.3 s sweep
budgets.why: Apple: about 5 ms of main-thread work per update for continuous interaction ('Improving app responsiveness'); at 60 updates a second that is 30% of a core, 1.3 s over the sweep.
